chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Uqba who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me in Al-Medina and I was praying, and I bent my head and I extended in my bowing, so he (peace be upon him) sent a message to me: ‘Do not do it’.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam instruct regarding excessive bowing during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s correction of excessive physical exertion in prayer, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (moderation) and avoiding *ghuluw* (exaggeration) in ritual acts. It underscores that while bowing is a pillar of prayer, it should be performed with dignity and balance rather than extreme contortion, a principle derived from the Prophet’s and Imams’ own practice.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Uqba who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassanasws saw me in Al-Medina and I was praying Salāt, and I bent my head and I extended in my Rukū (bowing), so heasws sent a message to me: ‘Do not do it’’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah who has said the following: “

Once abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saw me, in al-Madinah when I performed Salah (prayer). I bent down my head and stretched in my Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees). He (the Imam) sent me a message that said, ‘You must not do so (when you are in Ruku‘).’” (Ahadith 2-9 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
